passage:
A map in a geography book placed one country in the center. Another map from a different country placed another region in the center.
Students asked which map was correct.
The teacher explained that a round Earth must be shown on flat paper, so maps always involve choices. Center, size, and shape can change how people imagine importance.
The class looked at several world maps and discussed perspective.
They learned that maps are useful, but not neutral windows. They are designed views.
A map can help people understand the world, but it can also quietly teach them where they think the center is.
